name: Neural Baking with Latent-Space In-Scattering
definition: A rendering method that approximates indirect illumination (high-order scattering) by baking the in-scattering operator $\mathcal{K}$ into a compressed latent space representation of the radiance field, avoiding explicit integration and reducing model complexity compared to direct density-to-radiance mapping.
summary: Neural Baking with Latent-Space In-Scattering approximates indirect illumination by baking the in-scattering operator into a compressed latent space, avoiding explicit Radiative Transfer Equation integration for faster rendering.
